newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Northern Irish firms join Irish share index.
newsitem.headline: Northern Irish firms join Irish share index.

text.p: Ireland's main share index expanded on Thursday to include Northern Irish companies for the first time, boosting its total market capitalisation by seven percent.
Seven Northern Irish companies joined the Irish Stock Exchange's ISEQ index, which previously included only shares of companies based in the Irish Republic.

The Northern Irish firms were already traded on the Dublin exchange, under stock exchange dual-listing rules which allow shares of Irish firms to trade in both London and Dublin, but until now they were not included in the calculation of the ISEQ.
"This will make the Northern Ireland companies more tradeable on the Irish market," Irish Stock Exchange chief executive Tom Healy told Reuters.
"Companies which track the ISEQ will have to include them in full weight so holdings in them will have to be built up, although to a large extent this may already have happened," he said.
"Previously these firms were in limbo here, traded but not included in the index."
The largest two firms to join were Northern Ireland Electricity and engineering firm Powerscreen International, which will each have a weighting of 2.41 percent in the expanded index.
The biggest Irish shares in the index, such as AIB and Bank of Ireland, have weightings of more than 10 percent.
The other new members are Ulster Television, property firm Ewart, packaging firm Boxmore International, retailer Hampden Group and textile firm Lamont Holdings.
Engineering firm Mackie International is due to join the index later this year.
